    exists_pairOfDefinitionNonempty (PairOfDefinition A)There exists a pair of definition.  : NonemptyNonempty.{u} (α : Sort u) : Prop`Nonempty α` is a typeclass that says that `α` is not an empty type,
that is, there exists an element in the type. It differs from `Inhabited α`
in that `Nonempty α` is a `Prop`, which means that it does not actually carry
an element of `α`, only a proof that *there exists* such an element.
Given `Nonempty α`, you can construct an element of `α` *nonconstructively*
using `Classical.choice`.

    vle_mul_cancel : ∀ {xA yA zA : AType u_1}, ¬Not (a : Prop) : Prop`Not p`, or `¬p`, is the negation of `p`. It is defined to be `p → False`,
so if your goal is `¬p` you can use `intro h` to turn the goal into
`h : p ⊢ False`, and if you have `hn : ¬p` and `h : p` then `hn h : False`
and `(hn h).elim` will prove anything.

Let (A, A^{+}) be an affinoid ring (Definition 3.1). The adic spectrum is \mathrm{Spa}(A, A^{+}) = \{ v \in \mathrm{Cont}(A) : v(f) \le 1 \text{ for all } f \in A^{+} \}, the continuous valuations bounded by 1 on A^{+} (Definition 2.1). In Adic-Spaces this is \texttt{ValuationSpectrum.Spa} (with the integral subring packaged by the class \texttt{PlusSubring}). This is the fundamental functor of Huber's theory. Following Wedhorn Definition 7.23.

For a topological ring A, a subring A^{+} \subseteq A is a ring of integral elements (\texttt{IsRingOfIntegralElements}) if it is open, integrally closed in A, and contained in the power-bounded subring A^{\circ} (Definition 1.1). The pair (A, A^{+}) is then an affinoid ring (Huber pair). Following Wedhorn Definition 7.14.

A topological ring A is a Huber ring (or f-adic ring) if it admits a pair of definition: an open subring A_0 \subseteq A together with a finitely generated ideal I \subseteq A_0 such that the subspace topology on A_0 equals the I-adic topology — equivalently, the powers I^n form a neighbourhood basis of 0 in A_0. In Adic-Spaces the pair is the structure \texttt{PairOfDefinition} and the predicate is the class \texttt{IsHuberRing}. Following Wedhorn §6.

(Tate's acyclicity theorem / the structure sheaf.) For a strongly noetherian Tate ring, the structure presheaf \mathcal{O}_X on the rational subsets of X = \mathrm{Spa}(A, A^{+}) (Definition 3.2, Definition 4.1) is a sheaf: the Čech complex of a rational cover is exact (Tate acyclicity), so sections glue. This makes (\mathrm{Spa}(A, A^{+}), \mathcal{O}_X) an adic space. In Adic-Spaces: \texttt{structurePresheaf\_isSheaf} (Adic spaces/StructureSheaf.lean) — in progress (the Laurent-cover acyclicity and the gluing refinement carry the remaining sorrys).

The Tate algebra A\langle X \rangle over a Tate ring A (Definition 1.2) is the ring of restricted power series — those whose coefficients tend to 0 — the building block of the structure sheaf on rational subsets of \mathrm{Spa}(A, A^{+}). In Adic-Spaces this is \texttt{TateAlgebra}. Following Wedhorn Definition 7.29.

A Tate ring is a Huber ring (Definition 1.1) that contains a topologically nilpotent unit u \in A^\times with u^n \to 0 — a pseudo-uniformiser, the role of a uniformising parameter in non-archimedean geometry. In Adic-Spaces this is the class \texttt{IsTateRing}. Following Wedhorn Definition 6.10.

The valuation spectrum \mathrm{Spv}(A) of a commutative ring A is the set of equivalence classes of valuations on A. A point is presented as a valuative relation; the topology is generated by the basic open sets \mathrm{Spv}(A)(f/s) = \{ v : v(f) \le v(s) \ne 0 \}, and the support map v \mapsto \{a : v(a) = 0\} is continuous into \mathrm{Spec}(A). In Adic-Spaces these are \texttt{ValuationSpectrum}, \texttt{basicOpen}, and \texttt{supp}. Following Wedhorn Definition 4.1.
